entries.name: TANGZU Wan'er DSP
entries.verdict: Axel: top pick under $30, especially the DSP version with app EQ; balanced default tuning, one of the better entry-level options.
entries.quote: The 3.5 mm is nice, but the DSP version is amazing.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: 7Hz x Crinacle Zero 2
entries.verdict: Axel: bassier pick under $30; good bass, non-fatiguing treble, tamer upper midrange than the Chu 2.
entries.quote: There's the 7Hz x Crinacle Zero 2 and the Moondrop Chu 2. Both sound great, both have good amount of bass and non-fatiguing treble.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Moondrop Chu 2
entries.verdict: Axel: bassier pick under $30; good bass, non-fatiguing treble, metal shell and more forward vocals than the Zero 2.
entries.quote: The Chu 2 has a metal shell and more forward vocals, while the Zero 2 has a tamer upper midrange.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Tripowin x Zero DB Vivacity
entries.verdict: Axel: another good set under $30, with more bass, warmth and detail and a smoother sound.
entries.quote: Another good set at this price is going to be the Tripowin x Zero DB Vivacity. This one has a bit more bass, a bit more warmth and detail, and a smoother overall sound.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Cadenza
entries.verdict: Axel: top pick under $50; warm, bassy all-rounder with good detail and treble extension.
entries.quote: And in this range, uh the Kiwi Ears Cadenza is going to be my top pick. It's a great all-rounder, it's warm, a bit warm, has a bassy uh sound signature, good amount of detail, good treble extension
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: DUNU Titan S
entries.verdict: Axel: vocal pick at $50-100; natural sound, less warm than the other options.
entries.quote: As for vocals, I'm going to recommend at this price point the DUNU Titan S. It's still a great pick for vocals, natural sound, less warm than the other options.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Yincrow X6 V2 Defined
entries.verdict: Axel: balanced, fun pick at $50-100; mild V-shape, textured bass, forward mids, amazing value.
entries.quote: I'm going to recommend the Yincrow X6 V2 Defined. It's got a mild V-shaped sound signature, great texture in the bass, forward mids, good detail, modular cable, just an amazing value uh all around.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: AFUL Explorer
entries.verdict: Axel: bassy-warm pick at $100-200; relaxed, great sub-bass, smooth treble, easy for long sessions.
entries.quote: I'll start with the AFUL Explorer. Now, this one is a bit warm, relaxed, and very comfortable. Uh it's got great sub-bass extension, textured low end, punchy bass, smooth treble, and really easy to listen to for long listening sessions.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: DUNU Kima 2
entries.verdict: Axel: warm like the Explorer but with more forward, clearer vocals and less sub-bass.
entries.quote: If you want something still warm, but with more forward vocals, we're going to have the DUNU Kima 2. It's got less sub-bass than the Explorer, but we get more vocal forwardness and clarity.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: TANGZU FUDU
entries.verdict: Axel: vocal/midrange pick at $100-200; beautiful midrange, very natural timbre.
entries.quote: I'm going to recommend the Tangzu Fudu. It's a standout at this price point. It has a beautiful-sounding midrange, very natural timbre, comes with modular cable as well.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: TANGZU Wu Zetian
entries.verdict: Axel: vocal pick at $200-300; amazing timbre, natural midrange, premium build.
entries.quote: And for vocals, I'm going to add in the Tangzu Wu Zetian. Again, amazing timbre, natural-sounding midrange, and it has a premium build.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Softears Volume S
entries.verdict: Axel: one of his top vocal picks at $300-400; natural mids, textured bass, smooth and safe treble.
entries.quote: At this price point, there is the Softears Volume 7. And this one has the natural-sounding midrange, the beautiful bass, you know, great bass texture and physicality, very smooth and safe treble, one of my picks top picks for vocals.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Punch Audio Martillo
entries.verdict: Axel: bass pick at $300-400; amazing bass physicality, detailed treble, recommended for bassheads.
entries.quote: if you love bass, you have to check out really the Punch Audio Martillo. Amazing bass, uh great bass physicality, great detail in the treble, super fun, and recommended for bass lovers and bassheads out there.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Softears Studio 4
entries.verdict: Axel: neutral/vocal pick; more reference and accurate than the Volume, less bass, very natural midrange.
entries.quote: I'm going to recommend the Softears Studio 4. This one is kind of like more reference, less space, less warm, more accurate-sounding than the Volume 7. It's also great for vocals.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Xenns Mangird Top Pro
entries.verdict: Axel: pick at $400-500; benchmark-level, detailed balanced tonality, strong separation, one of the best all-rounders under $500.
entries.quote: it's going to be the Zens T Pro, which is a benchmark-level IEM, excellent detailed balanced tonality, strong separation.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Softears RSV
entries.verdict: Axel: vocal pick at $500-1,000; natural vocals, smooth treble.
entries.quote: there is the Softears RSV. This will be our vocal section. Has the natural vocals, the smooth treble.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: DUNU SA6 MKII
entries.verdict: Axel: option at $500-1,000; QDC-style tonality, bass switch, airy treble.
entries.quote: And there are other options like the DUNU SA6 Mark II, has that QDC-style tonality, has a bass switch, and an airy treble.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: DUNU Glacier
entries.verdict: Axel: over-$1,000 pick for Harman lovers; clean sub-bass, clean forward vocals, ultra-refined treble, very detailed.
entries.quote: then the DUNU Glacier takes it up a notch. It has that sub-bass, the clean mids, and the ultra-refined treble, uh very ethereal in its sound, and very detailed.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: AFUL Dawn X
entries.verdict: Axel: over-$1,000 pick for AFUL house-sound fans; more refined, detailed and balanced.
entries.quote: then for example, the AFUL Dawn X is a refined take on that sound, better detailed, better balanced overall.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Elysian Apostle
entries.verdict: Axel: over-$1,000 pick; fun, deep controlled bass and extended, airy, non-fatiguing EST treble.
entries.quote: then there is the Elysian Apostle, you know, it's it's that type of IEM that sounds fun. It's got a deep, controlled bass, you know, and that legendary EST treble that's incredibly extended and airy, non-fatiguing treble is so refined on this set.
entries.videoTitle: Top IEM Picks for Every Price Range

entries.name: Colorfly Silver Reference
entries.verdict: Axel: solid, easygoing sound, but the sharp-edged metal shell hurt his ears; try before buying.
entries.quote: Because of the fit, I can't fully recommend them. I think a lot of people might run into the same problem. But if you are curious about them, I recommend you try them out for yourselves.
entries.videoTitle: CrinEar Daybreak, BGVP Solomon & More

entries.name: ZIIGAAT LUSH
entries.verdict: Axel: natural, neutral-warm and completely non-fatiguing; vocals slightly back, not for bassheads; even works with metal.
entries.quote: But if you want something neutral, warm, something easy to listen to for hours, completely non-fatiguing, I feel the Zut Lush is definitely worth a look.
entries.videoTitle: CrinEar Daybreak, BGVP Solomon & More

entries.name: CRINEAR DAYBREAK
entries.verdict: Axel (no final verdict yet): mid-centric, forward and sometimes intense mids, smooth upper treble; wished for stronger technical performance.
entries.quote: That said, I do wish the technical performance was a bit stronger here. And I have heard that there is a specific ear tip that can improve the Daybreak sound. So, I want to try that first before giving my final verdict.
entries.videoTitle: CrinEar Daybreak, BGVP Solomon & More

entries.name: BGVP Solomon
entries.verdict: Axel (impressions): bass and treble boosted; slamming bass, bright treble with lots of EST shimmer, excellent resolution and separation.
entries.quote: Okay, technically the Solomon has excellent resolution, details pop, and it has fantastic separation across the whole frequency spectrum from the bass, mids, and treble.
entries.videoTitle: CrinEar Daybreak, BGVP Solomon & More

entries.name: ooopusX op.22
entries.verdict: Axel: a skip; thin, sometimes artificial vocals and bright, harsh treble; bass mode adds muddiness.
entries.quote: So, overall, I don't like the sound of this IEM.
entries.videoTitle: I\O Cielo, OoopusX Op.22, & Truthear KeyX

entries.name: IO CIELO TW51 Stock
entries.verdict: Axel: smooth, chill, slightly warm and full with a natural, rich midrange; 4-7k can bite on energetic tracks; not the most technical.
entries.quote: This is how I hear the Cielo. It has a smooth, chill, slightly warm, and full sound. It's a bit forgiving, not the most technical, but the detail is there. The natural midrange and rich tonality is what makes it enjoyable.
entries.videoTitle: I\O Cielo, OoopusX Op.22, & Truthear KeyX

entries.name: Softears RSV mk2
entries.verdict: Axel: likes it; the 5-7k dip removes treble harshness for him, with stronger sub-bass and more natural percussion.
entries.quote: And then, we have the Softears RSV Mark II. I like that set. One thing I like about Softears IEMs is, you can see on the graph, there's like a dip between 5 to 7k, and I like that, it works for my ear.
entries.videoTitle: I\O Cielo, OoopusX Op.22, & Truthear KeyX

entries.name: Kefine Arnar
entries.verdict: Axel: not a fan; good bass and build, but dark, muted, recessed treble and underwhelming technicalities for the price.
entries.quote: Overall, I'm not a fan of the sound. I don't find it enjoyable from being completely honest. I like the bass, I like the accessories, the build quality is very nice, that metal build quality that I expect from Kinera. Just the sound is dark, a bit muted, and very niche.
entries.videoTitle: Kefine Arnar, Tin T6 & Tin P2 Ultra

entries.name: TinHiFi T6
entries.verdict: Axel: solid, bassy-warm set with strong sub-bass; treble could be smoother; competes on sale.
entries.quote: Overall, it's still a solid set. I like the bass, I like the build. The mids are reasonable. Treble could definitely be smoother. It's kind of harder to recommend when some alternatives sound better for less, but on sale, it competes with its peers.
entries.videoTitle: Kefine Arnar, Tin T6 & Tin P2 Ultra

entries.name: TinHiFi P2 Ultra
entries.verdict: Axel: very bright, splashy and sibilant with planar timbre; below-average technicalities; not competitive today.
entries.quote: Even against hybrids in the $300 to $500 range, the difference is night and day. The sound quality just isn't there. Sound-wise, it's just not competing with planar IEMs today.
entries.videoTitle: Kefine Arnar, Tin T6 & Tin P2 Ultra

entries.name: GeekWold GK20 Pro
entries.verdict: Axel: nasal, thin mids and very bright, metallic treble; unnatural timbre.
entries.quote: The sound of this IM has issues and I'll just leave it at that.
entries.videoTitle: EPZ P40, Melody Wings Venus & GK20 Pro

entries.name: Melody Wings Venus
entries.verdict: Axel: treble-focused and fatiguing (5k peak), sibilant; only the imaging impressed him.
entries.quote: Overall, this IM sounds odd and fatiguing. Even the vocals sound off. I'm sure some people enjoy it, but I'm not one of them.
entries.videoTitle: EPZ P40, Melody Wings Venus & GK20 Pro

entries.name: EPZ P40
entries.verdict: Axel: Harman 2019 with a treble boost; clean, forward vocals, quick clean bass, lots of smooth treble; great build and cable.
entries.quote: Yeah, if you're into a Harmon style sound with bright treble and you want an IM with good build, field resin shell, a modular cable, the EPZ P40 is definitely worth checking out.
entries.videoTitle: EPZ P40, Melody Wings Venus & GK20 Pro

entries.name: Sivga Que UTG
entries.verdict: Axel (first impressions): skip; much less of the original Que's rich bass, boomy bass bleeding into vocals, bright peaky treble.
entries.quote: And yeah, I'm sad to say, guys, that this is a skip for me.
entries.videoTitle: MANY NEW IEMS!! (Top Pro, FX17, & more)

entries.name: Astrotec Archimedes
entries.verdict: Axel (first impressions): skip; muffled, veiled, recessed vocals and dull treble.
entries.quote: I tried like four different tracks and this one unfortunately is also a skip. Like this one doesn't sound good.
entries.videoTitle: MANY NEW IEMS!! (Top Pro, FX17, & more)

entries.name: DUNU Titan X
entries.verdict: Host: one of the better V-shaped sets at about $35; a fun, bassier starting point, not neutral.
entries.quote: These have a V-shaped presentation, and for this price point, I do really consider this to be one of the better V-shaped tuned sets out there.
entries.videoTitle: MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS - SUMMER SALE!!

entries.name: AFUL Performer 5+2
entries.verdict: Host: still a favourite; mild V-shape with a tasteful bass boost and very good technicalities.
entries.quote: It does have a little more of a bass boost, but it is very tastefully done. It's technical performance is still what I would consider to be very good at this price point.
entries.videoTitle: MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS - SUMMER SALE!!

entries.name: Binary EP321
entries.verdict: Host: well-done neutral but bright tuning with some of the best technicalities in its price range.
entries.quote: But, if you like a brighter set with excellent technical performance, and I mean some of the best in this price range, uh then this could be a really good option for you.
entries.videoTitle: MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS - SUMMER SALE!!

entries.name: DUNU 242
entries.verdict: Host: neutral with forward upper mids; a great vocal set with natural, focused, textured vocals.
entries.quote: I think if you are a vocal lover, this set does vocals very, very well. Uh that's probably one of my favorite things about this set. Vocals just sound very natural, very focused, very textured.
entries.videoTitle: MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS - SUMMER SALE!!

entries.name: DUNU 142
entries.verdict: Host: U-shaped, a bit more fun than neutral without losing naturalness; a good all-rounder with very good technicalities.
entries.quote: It's a little more of a fun presentation, but it does that without sacrificing naturalness.
entries.videoTitle: MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS RIGHT NOW!

entries.name: Juzear Harrier
entries.verdict: Host: his top IEM in its price range; neutral with a bass boost, versatile.
entries.quote: To me, it basically sounds again exactly the way they describe it, neutral with a bass boost.
entries.videoTitle: MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS RIGHT NOW!

entries.name: AFUL Performer5
entries.verdict: Host: long his favourite $200 IEM; AFUL house sound, smooth and balanced with solid technicalities.
entries.quote: And again, good sound does not expire. This was my favorite $200 IEM for a really long time and I still listen to this.
entries.videoTitle: MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS RIGHT NOW!

entries.name: Binary x Gizaudio Chopin
entries.verdict: Host (a Gizaudio collaboration): Harman-style with more mid-bass; outstanding bass quality, natural mids and treble.
entries.quote: Again, another example of an older set that is in my in my opinion still a great set even by today's standards. The bass quality is still outstanding.
entries.videoTitle: MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS RIGHT NOW!

entries.name: AFUL MagicOne
entries.verdict: Dave: single-BA budget set with a solid, slightly warm tuning and good extension both ways.
entries.quote: And somehow they've managed to not only create an IM that covers the full frequency spectrum, but also give it a really solid tuning as well, especially for this price point.
entries.videoTitle: 2025! 10 SUMMER DEALS ON IEMs AND DACs!!

entries.name: Juzear x Z Reviews Defiant
entries.verdict: Dave: close to the Performer 5+2's neutral sound, edging toward V-shape, and a bit more vocal-forward.
entries.quote: However, it is kind of edging very closely to a V-shaped presentation. So, it's a little more fun and maybe just a little more engaging. However, the Defiant is a little more vocal forward than the 5 Plus 2.
entries.videoTitle: 2025! 10 SUMMER DEALS ON IEMs AND DACs!!

entries.name: Elysian Pilgrim
entries.verdict: Dave: favourite mid-tier set; neutral-ish U-shape with some of the best technicalities under $500.
entries.quote: So, if you are looking for a neutralish U-shaped tuned IM with outstanding technical performance, and I mean some of the best technical performance under $500 at this price point, this is absolutely a no-brainer in my opinion.
entries.videoTitle: 2025! 10 SUMMER DEALS ON IEMs AND DACs!!

entries.name: Juzear Butterfly 61T
entries.verdict: Dave: his favourite under $200; U-shaped, natural relaxed vocals, unusually detailed treble.
entries.quote: Plus, its treble presentation for this price point is unusually detailed and refined.
entries.videoTitle: 2025! 10 SUMMER DEALS ON IEMs AND DACs!!

entries.name: Kefine Delci
entries.verdict: Dave: one of his top picks under $100; neutral rather than V-shaped, one of the most natural sets he owns at that price.
entries.quote: this is probably one of the most natural sets that I own under $100 so it's an unusually well-tuned set for this price point
entries.videoTitle: BLACK FRIDAY!! MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS!!

entries.name: Binary Dynaquattro
entries.verdict: Dave (a Gizaudio collaboration): close to his neutral-with-sub-bass-boost preference; forward upper mids, smoother treble.
entries.quote: and even at its regular price I think this is a very solid choice and now with the discounted price it's a no-brainer in my opinion
entries.videoTitle: BLACK FRIDAY!! MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS!!

entries.name: DUNU x Gizaudio Davinci
entries.verdict: Dave (a Gizaudio collaboration): his favourite at $300; very natural and smooth, with dynamic, punchy bass.
entries.quote: one of the many reasons I love the set so much is because it's probably one of the most natural and smoothest sets that I own under $500
entries.videoTitle: BLACK FRIDAY!! MY FAVORITE IEM AND DAC DEALS!!
